mainTopic: Whose תחום objects follow on יום טוב (guests' portions, deposits, רב חנא's meat), and which animals are מוקצה for slaughter
overview: The משנה rules that guests may not carry home food their host gave them on יום טוב, unless he transferred ownership to them on ערב יום טוב. The reason is that objects follow the 'feet' (the תחום) of whoever owned them when יום טוב began. The גמרא brings a dispute about produce left with a friend for safekeeping. רב says it follows the keeper, and שמואל says it follows the owner. A suggested link to a damages dispute between the חכמים and רבי is rejected by both. רב's view is then challenged from the משנה twice and defended with the idea of a 'corner set aside' for the owner, and also with the point that a full transfer of ownership is different. The story of רב חנא בר חנילאי's meat on the door bar raises several challenges. The גמרא finally rereads it as a question of meat left unwatched, not a question of תחום. A new משנה then teaches that household animals may be slaughtered on יום טוב but desert animals may not, because they are מוקצה. A ברייתא and רבי argue over how to define desert animals. The גמרא begins to ask whether רבי holds of מוקצה at all, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Guests may not carry home their portions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that guests who came to a host on יום טוב may not carry their food portions home unless the host transferred ownership to them before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone invited guests to his home, they may not carry the food portions home in their hands, unless he gave them ownership of their portions on ערב יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a rule: guests may not carry home the food their host gave them on יום טוב, unless the host gave it to them before יום טוב started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, an object may only be carried as far as its owner may walk. The food belonged to the host when יום טוב began, so it is limited by the host's walking boundary (תחום), even after it is given to the guests. If the host transferred it to them on ערב יום טוב, it was already theirs when יום טוב began, and it follows their boundary.

keyTerms.meaning: transferred ownership (often through a third person)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not carrying from one domain to another. The problem is the walking boundary (תחום): the food may only go where the person who owned it when יום טוב began may walk.

phrases.english: One who invited guests to his home —
they may not carry portions in their hands,
unless he transferred to them
their portions from the eve of the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁזִּמֵּן אֶצְלוֹ אוֹרְחִים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gifts given on יום טוב follow the תחום of the giver, unless ownership was transferred before יום טוב.

steps.title: Produce left with a friend: whose boundary?
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל disagree about produce left with a friend for safekeeping: does it follow the friend's boundary or the owner's?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone deposits produce with his friend, רב said it is like the feet of the one it was deposited with, and שמואל said it is like the feet of the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between רב and שמואל about produce that someone left with a friend to guard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that objects follow their owner's boundary. Now the question is what happens when the owner is one person and the guard is another. רב says the guard's boundary counts. שמואל says the owner's boundary counts.

keyTerms.meaning: one who deposits an item with someone else
like the feet of; follows the walking boundary of

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
One who deposits produce with his friend —

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: כְּרַגְלֵי מִי שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ לוֹ,
phrases.english: Rav said: like the feet of the one they were deposited with,
and Shmuel said: like the feet of the depositor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: הַמַּפְקִיד פֵּירוֹת אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's idea (objects follow their owner's feet) to a deposit, where the owner and the holder are different people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: deposited produce follows the שומר's תחום. שמואל: it follows the owner's תחום.

steps.title: Linking the dispute to a damages משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב and שמואל are following their known positions from another dispute, and quotes a משנה about damages in a courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that רב and שמואל follow their own reasoning. As we learned in a משנה: if he brought it in with permission, the owner of the courtyard is liable. רבי says: he is never liable until the homeowner accepts responsibility to guard it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that this dispute may be the same as an older one, and quotes that משנה. This sets up the next step, which shows how רב and שמואל ruled on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the quoted משנה, the חכמים say that letting someone bring things into your courtyard makes you responsible for them. רבי says you are responsible only if you clearly agreed to guard them. The idea is that the same question, how much permission makes an object 'yours', might decide the boundary question too.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (a suggested explanation that may be rejected)

phrases.english: Let us say that Rav and Shmuel
follow their own reasoning,
as we learned: if he brought it in with permission —
phrases.notes: This means bringing your produce or animal into someone else's courtyard with the owner's okay.

phrases.english: the owner of the courtyard is liable.
Rabbi says: he is never liable

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לִשְׁמוֹר.
phrases.english: until the homeowner accepts upon himself to guard.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָזְדוּ לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes that the dispute in step 2 grows out of an earlier dispute about damages.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute about the boundary of deposited produce really the same as the dispute between חכמים and רבי about courtyard liability?

steps.title: רב rules like חכמים, שמואל like רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports that רב ruled like the חכמים and שמואל ruled like רבי, so the גמרא suggests each one's boundary ruling follows that position.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows the חכמים. And שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי. So shall we say that רב follows the חכמים and שמואל follows רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב and שמואל ruled in the damages dispute, and finishes the suggestion: maybe each one's boundary ruling comes from his ruling there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds like the חכמים: permission is enough to make the host responsible, so the produce also counts as the holder's for the boundary. שמואל holds like רבי: permission alone does not make the object the holder's, so it still follows the owner. If this is right, the two disputes are really one.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said that Rav said:
the halacha follows the words of the Sages,
phrases.notes: The Sages here are the first opinion in that משנה: permission alone makes the courtyard owner liable.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: the halacha follows Rabbi.
Shall we say that Rav spoke like the Rabbis
and Shmuel spoke like Rabbi?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּנַן וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the suggestion from step 3 by showing how רב and שמואל ruled in the damages dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב's boundary ruling depend on the חכמים' view, and שמואל's on רבי's view?

steps.title: רב: my view works even according to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב rejects the link: רבי only said no liability when the host never agreed to guard, but a שומר has clearly agreed to guard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב can tell you: I hold my view even according to רבי. רבי only spoke there because, in a normal case, the host does not accept responsibility to guard. But here, the friend did accept responsibility to guard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. רב explains that his ruling does not depend on the חכמים, because even רבי would agree in a case of deposit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי required that the courtyard owner agree to guard. Plain permission to bring something in does not mean that. In our case the friend took the produce for the very purpose of guarding it, so even רבי would count it as his. That means the two disputes are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: [he] can say to you (introduces a defense)
he only said his view up to this point (limits a ruling to its case)

steps.whatToRemember: רב can hold that deposited produce follows the שומר's boundary even according to רבי, because a שומר clearly took on guarding. So the dispute between רב and שמואל does not have to match the damages dispute.

phrases.english: Rav can say to you:
I said it even according to Rabbi —

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi only said his ruling there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the courtyard case from the damages משנה.

phrases.english: because in an ordinary case
he did not accept upon himself the guarding,
but here —
he did accept upon himself the guarding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link proposed in steps 3 and 4 by pointing out a difference between the cases.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that רב must follow the חכמים. It does not decide the halacha between רב and שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion missed that a deposit is a case where the holder clearly agreed to guard, which is exactly what רבי requires.

steps.title: שמואל says his view works even according to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rejects the link to the courtyard dispute. The חכמים said the ox is in the courtyard owner's domain only because the ox's owner wants that, so he avoids paying for damage. Nobody wants his produce to be in someone else's boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל could say: My ruling holds even according to the חכמים. The חכמים only said what they said there because a person is happy to have his ox count as being in the courtyard owner's domain. That way, if it causes damage, he does not have to pay. But here, is a person happy to have his produce count as being in his friend's domain?!
steps.whatsHappening: Just as רב pushed away the link in Step 5, now שמואל pushes it away too. He says his ruling fits even the opinion of the חכמים, whom רב had followed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the courtyard case, being in the courtyard owner's domain helps the ox's owner, because he avoids paying for damage. With produce, being in the keeper's boundary only hurts the owner, because it limits where his food can go. Since the reasons are different, the two disputes are not connected.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said this much (their ruling is limited to that case)
It suits him / he is happy with it

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and שמואל have now shown that their positions do not depend on the courtyard-damage dispute. The suggested link from Steps 3–4 falls away.

phrases.english: And שמואל could say:
What I said holds even according to the חכמים —
phrases.notes: These are the חכמים from the courtyard-damage dispute in Step 3, whom רב followed.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם,
phrases.english: the חכמים only said their ruling there
because a person is happy
for his ox to stand in the domain of the courtyard owner,
so that if it damages him, he is not liable.
But here —
is a person happy
for his produce to stand in his friend's domain?!
phrases.notes: He means the produce would count as part of the keeper's boundary, which only limits the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 5: after רב separated himself from רבי, שמואל separates himself from the חכמים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggestion that שמואל's boundary ruling depends on following רבי in the damages dispute.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים' reason (the owner benefits by avoiding liability) does not apply to produce, where being in the friend's domain is a disadvantage.

steps.title: Challenge to רב: the משנה says produce follows an owner who made an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the owner made an עירוב, his produce goes where he goes. If deposited produce follows the keeper, as רב says, why should the owner's עירוב matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If he made an עירוב, his produce is like him. But if you say produce follows the boundary of the person it was deposited with, then even if the owner made an עירוב, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks רב's view using a line from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the produce to the owner's עירוב, which means the owner's boundary controls the produce. That fits שמואל, but under רב the produce should belong to the keeper's boundary, so the owner's עירוב should change nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He made an עירוב (extending his שבת/יום טוב walking boundary)
Like the feet of (follows the boundary of)

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: וְאִם עֵרַב הוּא — פֵּירוֹתָיו כָּמוֹהוּ.
phrases.english: We learned: And if he made an עירוב — his produce is like him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּרַגְלֵי מִי שֶׁהִפְקִידוּ אֶצְלוֹ,
phrases.english: But if you say it is like the feet of the one with whom they deposited it,
then if he made an עירוב, what difference does it make?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: וְאִם עֵרַב הוּא — פֵּירוֹתָיו כָּמוֹהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the link to the damages dispute set aside, the גמרא now tests רב directly against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that deposited produce follows the keeper's boundary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the owner's עירוב decisive for the produce, which only makes sense if the produce follows the owner.

steps.title: Answer: the keeper set aside a corner for the owner
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports that the students of רב answered: the משנה is talking about a case where the keeper gave the owner his own corner for the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said that the students of רב's study hall say: The משנה is talking about a case where the keeper set aside a corner of his house for the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב's students answer the challenge by limiting the משנה to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the keeper sets aside a corner just for the owner, he shows that the produce is not in his own domain. In that case, even רב agrees the produce follows the owner and his עירוב. The normal case, with no corner set aside, still follows the keeper.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of רב's study hall say

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רב changed his view. Deposited produce still normally follows the keeper. The set-aside corner is a special exception.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב:
phrases.english: רב הונא said: The students of רב's study hall say:
For example, where he set aside a corner for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב: כְּגוֹן שֶׁיִּחֵד לוֹ קֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7 by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to describe a normal deposit, so it would contradict רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes a keeper who set aside a corner for the owner, so the produce follows the owner even according to רב.

steps.title: Second challenge to רב: the guests' food portions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says guests may carry their portions home if the host handed ownership to them before יום טוב. If deposited items follow the keeper, the portions are still in the host's house, so why would that help?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone who invited guests — they may not carry portions home in their hands unless he gave them ownership of their portions before יום טוב. But if you say items follow the boundary of the person they were deposited with, then even if he gave them ownership through another person, what difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב, this time from the guests case in the משנה (Step 1).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after ownership passes to the guests, the food stays in the host's house until יום טוב, so it looks like an item deposited with the host. Under רב it should follow the host's boundary, yet the משנה lets the guests take it home.

keyTerms.meaning: Through another person (who acquires on their behalf)

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁזִּמֵּן אֶצְלוֹ אוֹרְחִים —
phrases.english: Come and hear: One who invited guests to his home —
phrases.notes: This is the line from the משנה we saw in Step 1.

phrases.english: they may not carry portions in their hands,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן זִכָּה לָהֶם מָנוֹתֵיהֶם
phrases.english: unless he transferred ownership of their portions to them
before יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּרַגְלֵי מִי שֶׁהִפְקִידוֹ אֶצְלוֹ,
phrases.english: But if you say it is like the feet of the one with whom it was deposited,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי זִכָּה לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר מַאי הָוֵי?
phrases.english: then if he transferred ownership to them through another person, what difference does it make?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מִי שֶׁזִּמֵּן אֶצְלוֹ אוֹרְחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is answered, a second challenge to רב comes from another part of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that deposited items follow the keeper's boundary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The portions remain in the host's house, so under רב they should follow the host. The משנה, however, lets them follow the guests.

steps.title: Answer: transferring ownership works like setting aside a corner
steps.stepSummary: Handing over ownership through someone else is treated like setting aside a corner for the guests, so the portions follow the guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: since he gave them ownership through another person, it is like a case where he set aside a corner for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge using the same idea it used in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By formally handing ownership to the guests, the host shows he does not want the food in his own domain. That is the same message as setting aside a corner. So even רב agrees the portions follow the guests' boundary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is comparable / it is like

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁזִּכָּה לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר —
phrases.english: Here too, since he transferred ownership to them through another person —

phrases.aramaic: כְּמִי שֶׁיִּחֵד לוֹ קֶרֶן זָוִית דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: it is like one who set aside a corner for him.
phrases.notes: This points back to the answer from רב's students in Step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁזִּכָּה לָהֶם עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 9 by applying the 'set-aside corner' answer of Step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The portions in the host's house seemed to be ordinary deposits, so they would follow the host.
steps.terutzMaskana: Transferring ownership counts like setting aside a corner, so the portions follow the guests.

steps.title: Another answer: transferring ownership is a different case
steps.stepSummary: Another way to answer: transferring ownership is not like a deposit at all, because the host's whole goal is to make the food fully the guests'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: transferring ownership is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, separate answer to the guests challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer compared the transfer to a set-aside corner. This answer says that when the host fully gives the food away, it is simply not a deposit case. The food belongs completely to the guests and follows their boundary, so רב's rule about deposits does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: רב's view survives both challenges from the משנה. Produce follows the owner when the keeper set aside a corner for it, or when ownership was fully handed over. Otherwise, deposited produce follows the keeper.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: transferring ownership is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: זִכָּה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Food given to guests but still in the host's house looked like a deposit with the host.
steps.terutzMaskana: A full transfer of ownership is a different kind of case, so the portions follow the guests.

steps.title: רב חנא's meat on the door bar and רב הונא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר חנילאי hung meat on his host's door bar. רב הונא ruled that he may take it if he hung it himself, but not if his hosts hung it for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר חנילאי hung meat on the bar of the door. He came before רב הונא, who told him: If you hung it, go take it. If they hung it for you, do not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life story and a ruling about whether a guest may carry his meat home on יום טוב. This ruling is what the next several steps will question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whose 'feet' the meat follows for the rules of תחום. רב הונא makes it depend on who hung it. If the guest hung it, it is his. If the hosts hung it, it stays with them.

keyTerms.meaning: the bar or side-post of the door

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Chanilai
hung meat on the bar of the door.
He came before Rav Huna.
He said to him: If you hung it,
go take it.
But if they hung it for you,
do not take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חָנָא בַּר חֲנִילַאי תְּלָא בִּשְׂרָא בְּעִבְרָא דְּדַשָּׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical story that ties into רב's rule about deposits, which was discussed in steps 7-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat the guest hung himself follows him. Meat the hosts hung for him does not.

steps.title: How can he take meat he hung himself, if deposits follow the keeper?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא was a student of רב, and רב holds that deposited items follow the one keeping them. So even meat the guest hung himself should follow the host.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he hung it himself, may he really take it? But רב הונא was a student of רב, and רב said: it is like the feet of the one it was deposited with!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first half of רב הונא's ruling, using his own teacher's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat sits in the host's house, so it is like a deposit there. By רב's rule, a deposit follows the host, not the owner. That should mean the guest cannot take it even if he hung it himself.

keyTerms.meaning: like the feet of; it may only go where this person may go
the one with whom it was deposited

phrases.english: And if he hung it, may he take it?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִיד דְּרַב הֲוָה,
phrases.english: But wasn't Rav Huna a student of Rav?
And Rav said:
It is like the feet of the one it was deposited with!
phrases.notes: This is the same rule of רב that the גמרא was working with in steps 7-11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִיהוּ תְּלָא מִי שָׁקֵיל? וְהָא רַב הוּנָא תַּלְמִיד דְּרַב הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of רב הונא's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the guest may take meat he hung himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A student would not argue with his teacher רב, and רב holds that deposits follow the keeper.

steps.title: The door bar counts like a corner set aside for him
steps.stepSummary: The door bar is different. Hanging meat there is like the host giving the guest his own corner, so the meat follows the guest.
steps.simpleTranslation: The door bar is different, because it is like someone who set aside a corner for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by using the 'own corner' idea from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the guest gets a specific spot of his own, his things there are not treated as a deposit with the host. The door bar is that kind of spot. So meat the guest hung there follows his feet.

phrases.english: The bar of the door is different,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְמִי שֶׁיִּחֵד לוֹ קֶרֶן זָוִית דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: because it is like one who set aside a corner for him.
phrases.notes: This is the same 'own corner' answer רב's students gave back in step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי עִבְרָא דְּדָשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the door bar is treated like a private corner
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meat in the host's house is a deposit and follows the host.
steps.terutzMaskana: The door bar works like a designated corner, so meat the guest hung there follows him, and רב הונא agrees with רב after all.

steps.title: רב הלל challenges from שמואל's ox of a fattener
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל asks why the guest cannot take meat the hosts hung for him. שמואל said a fattener's ox follows the feet of everyone, meaning whoever ends up with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הלל said to רב אשי: And if they hung it for him, may he really not take it? But שמואל said: A fattener's ox is like the feet of every person!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא attacks the second half of רב הונא's ruling, that the guest may not take meat the hosts hung for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fattener raises oxen to sell, so from before יום טוב the ox is meant for whoever buys it, and it follows the buyer. In the same way, the hosts hung the meat with the plan that the guest would take it. So it should follow the guest.

keyTerms.meaning: an ox of a fattener, someone who fattens oxen to sell for meat
like the feet of every person; it follows whoever gets it
but didn't he say? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִינְהוּ תָּלוּ לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל?
phrases.english: And if they hung it for him, may he not take it?
But didn't Shmuel say:
An ox of a fattener
is like the feet of every person.
phrases.notes: In other words, it follows whoever buys it on יום טוב, because it was always meant to be sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְאִי אִינְהוּ תָּלוּ לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the second half of רב הונא's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the guest may not take meat the hosts hung for him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that something meant from the start for a future recipient follows that recipient. The meat was meant for the guest, so it should follow him.

steps.title: רבינא challenges from the halacha like רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings another challenge. רבי יוחנן ruled the halacha follows רבי דוסא, who holds that something certain to go to a person follows that person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: And if they hung it for him, may he really not take it? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבי דוסא!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge against the same ruling, this time from a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי דוסא holds that in a town with one shepherd, an animal that will surely be given to him follows the shepherd. The meat hung for the guest is just as certainly his. So it should follow him.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִינְהוּ תָּלוּ לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל?
phrases.english: And if they hung it for him, may he not take it?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Dosa.
phrases.notes: רבי דוסא's case: in a town with only one shepherd, an animal that will be given to him follows the shepherd's feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְאִי אִינְהוּ תָּלוּ לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge alongside רב הלל's in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the guest may not take meat the hosts hung for him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted halacha follows רבי דוסא: something certain to reach a person follows that person. The meat was certainly meant for the guest.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges from the משנה about animals and vessels
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב כהנא the same question, using the משנה that animals and vessels follow their owner. Meat hung for the guest should follow him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: And if they hung it for him, may he really not take it? But we learned in a משנה: Animals and vessels are like the feet of their owners!
steps.whatsHappening: A third challenge against the same ruling, this time from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a person's belongings follow the owner's feet. The meat belongs to the guest, so it should follow him even if the hosts did the hanging. The next step answers all three challenges at once with a new reading of the story.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's ruling has two halves. The first half (he may take meat he hung himself) was defended by the 'own corner' idea. The second half (he may not take meat the hosts hung) now faces three challenges: שמואל's fattener's ox, רבי דוסא, and the משנה about animals and vessels. The next step answers all three.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִינְהוּ תָּלוּ לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל?
phrases.english: And if they hung it for him, may he not take it?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
Animals and vessels are like the feet of the owners!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: וְאִי אִינְהוּ תָּלוּ לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third challenge after steps 15 and 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the guest may not take meat the hosts hung for him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that a person's belongings follow the owner. The meat is the guest's, so it should follow him.

steps.title: A new reading of רב חנא's case: it was about paying attention to the meat
steps.stepSummary: Because of all the questions, the גמרא reads the story differently. The issue was not which owner the meat follows. The issue was whether רב חנא בר חנילאי, a great scholar busy with his learning, kept his mind on his meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חנא בר חנילאי is different. He is a great man who is busy with his learning. So רב הונא told him: if you hung the meat yourself, you have a sign on it and you never took your mind off it, so go take it. But if they hung it for you, you took your mind off it, so do not take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up its earlier explanation of the story and offers a completely new one that avoids all the questions from steps 13–17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier challenges assumed the story was about whose place the meat 'follows.' Now the גמרא says the issue was meat that was out of sight and not watched. If רב חנא hung it himself, he knows a sign on it and kept it in mind, so it is fine. If others hung it, he never paid attention to it, so he may not take it.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, a big scholar
Busy and absorbed in his learning
You took your mind off it, you stopped paying attention

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רב חנא בר חנילאי ends up being about watching the meat, not about whose place the meat follows.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't keep reading this case as being about whose place the meat follows. The word אֶלָּא tells you the גמרא is dropping that whole approach and starting over with a different explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers all the questions in steps 13–17 at once, because they were all built on the old explanation.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, שָׁאנֵי רַב חָנָא בַּר חֲנִילַאי —
phrases.english: Rather, רב חנא בר חנילאי is different
for he is a great man and busy with his learning
and this is what he said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב הונא, who gave the ruling in the story.

phrases.english: If you hung it,
you have a sign on it
and you did not take your mind off it,
go take it.
But if they hung it for you,
you took your mind off it,
so do not take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שָׁאנֵי רַב חָנָא בַּר חֲנִילַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers all the questions in steps 13–17 by reading the story in a completely new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the case: a different issue is at play
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling was about whose place the meat follows, host or guest.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling was about whether a busy scholar kept his mind on the meat. Meat he hung himself is fine; meat others hung for him is not.

steps.title: משנה: household animals may be slaughtered on יום טוב, desert animals may not
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: on יום טוב one may water and slaughter animals that sleep in town, but not animals that sleep out in the pasture.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not water and slaughter desert animals on יום טוב, but one may water and slaughter household animals. Household animals are ones that sleep in the town. Desert animals are ones that sleep in the pasture.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: which animals may be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Desert animals live far out in the pasture, so a person does not have them in mind for יום טוב. That makes them מוקצה. Household animals sleep in town and are ready to use. The משנה defines the two groups by where they sleep at night.

keyTerms.meaning: Desert animals that live out in the pasture
Household animals that sleep in town

phrases.english: משנה:
One may not water and slaughter desert animals,
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about יום טוב, even though it doesn't say so here.

phrases.english: but one may water and slaughter household animals.
These are household animals: those that sleep in the town.
Desert animals: those that sleep in the pasture.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַשְׁקִין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַמִּדְבָּרִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the meat discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, household animals (which sleep in town) may be watered and slaughtered; desert animals (which sleep in the pasture) may not.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention watering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה adds the word "water" when the topic is only slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to say "water and slaughter"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about an extra word in the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is teaching which animals are מוקצה for slaughtering. Watering seems to have nothing to do with that, so why is it mentioned?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking about an extra word)

phrases.english: גמרא:
Why do I need it to say
"water and slaughter"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר מַשְׁקִין וְשׁוֹחֲטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה mention watering when its topic is slaughtering?

steps.title: A practical tip: water the animal before slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה slips in a practical lesson: water the animal first, so the skin comes off the meat more easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה teaches us something along the way: a person should give his animal water and then slaughter it, because otherwise the skin sticks to the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the word "water" is there to teach a practical lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word is not part of the מוקצה rule. It is a side lesson about how to slaughter: an animal that was given water first is easier to skin, because the hide doesn't stick to the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: Along the way, taught as a side point
The skin sticking to the meat

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us something along the way,
that a person should give his animal water
and then slaughter it,
because of the skin sticking.
phrases.notes: Without water first, the hide sticks to the meat and is hard to peel off.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Water" teaches a practical side lesson: water the animal before slaughtering so the skin comes off easily.

steps.title: ברייתא: how the תנא קמא defines desert and household animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a fuller definition. Desert animals stay out in the pasture from פסח until the first rain. Household animals graze outside the תחום but come back to sleep inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Which are desert animals and which are household animals? Desert animals go out at פסח time, graze in the pasture, and come back in at the first rainfall. Household animals go out and graze outside the תחום, but come back and sleep inside the תחום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's two groups in more detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says desert animals are out the whole summer, from פסח until the first rain. Household animals may graze far away during the day, but as long as they return to sleep inside the תחום, they count as household animals.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall at the start of the rainy season
The town's boundary for walking on שבת and יום טוב

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן מִדְבָּרִיּוֹת וְאֵלּוּ הֵן בַּיָּיתוֹת.
phrases.english: Which are desert animals and which are household animals?
Desert animals: all that go out at פסח time
and graze in the pasture,
and come back in at the first rainfall.
And these are household animals:
all that go out and graze outside the boundary,
and come and sleep inside the boundary.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵלּוּ הֵן מִדְבָּרִיּוֹת וְאֵלּוּ הֵן בַּיָּיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that defines the משנה's terms more fully.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Desert animals stay out from פסח until the first rain. Household animals graze outside the תחום but sleep inside it.

steps.title: רבי: only animals that never come into town are desert animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי disagrees. He says both groups from the ברייתא are household animals. Only animals that never come into the settled area, summer or winter, are desert animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: both of these groups are household animals. Rather, desert animals are those that go out and graze in the pasture and never come into the settled area, not in the summer and not in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different opinion from the תנא קמא about which animals count as desert animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, animals that are out all summer are desert animals. רבי says that since those animals come home in the rainy season, they still count as household animals and may be slaughtered. Only animals that never come into town at all are מוקצה.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא: animals out all summer are desert animals. רבי: only animals that never come into town are desert animals.

phrases.english: רבי says:
Both these and those are household animals.
phrases.notes: "Both" means the summer-pasture animals and the ones that sleep in town.

phrases.english: Rather, these are desert animals:
all that go out and graze in the pasture,
and do not come into the settled area,
not in the summer
and not in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ בַּיָּיתוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's definition in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only animals that never come into the settled area at any time of year are desert animals. All the others are household animals.

steps.title: Does רבי accept the idea of מוקצה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי holds of מוקצה, since his definition of desert animals seems to rely on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי really hold of מוקצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's opinion from step 23. It asks whether he even holds of מוקצה. This question sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Desert animals may not be slaughtered on יום טוב because nobody planned to use them, so they are מוקצה. When רבי argues about which animals count as desert animals, he seems to agree that this category is forbidden. The גמרא now asks whether that fits with what we know about רבי's view on מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside in a person's mind, so it may not be used or moved on שבת or יום טוב
And does he hold of...? (an opening that questions someone's position)

phrases.english: And does רבי hold of muktze?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 23. רבי's definition of desert animals only makes sense if those animals are forbidden as מוקצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רבי's statement in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's opinion in step 23 about desert animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's definition assumes desert animals are forbidden as מוקצה, but he may not hold of מוקצה at all

steps.title: רבי's son asks him about unripe dates
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a story. רבי's son asked about unripe dates set aside to ripen, and רבי answered that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי שמעון the son of רבי ask רבי: Unripe dates put away to ripen, what is the law according to רבי שמעון? He answered him: According to רבי שמעון there is no מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the evidence for its question. It tells of a question רבי's son asked him and the answer רבי gave. The proof is not finished yet; the גמרא's line continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unripe dates put away to ripen cannot be eaten yet, so a person does not plan to use them on שבת or יום טוב. That makes them a clear test case for מוקצה. רבי's answer gives רבי שמעון's view that there is no מוקצה, and the גמרא will use this exchange to show what רבי himself thinks.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it true that... (brings a source that challenges what was just said)
He asked him (a question to a teacher)
Unripe dates, put away to ripen

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רבי שמעון here. The one asking is רבי שמעון the son of רבי. The one whose opinion he asks about is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, the famous תנא who does not hold of מוקצה.

phrases.english: But didn't he ask
רבי שמעון the son of רבי ask רבי:
Unripe dates (put away to ripen)
What is the law according to רבי שמעון?
phrases.notes: This רבי שמעון is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, not the son who is asking.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מוּקְצֶה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: He said to him: There is no muktze according to רבי שמעון

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the challenge raised in step 24
steps.raayaObject: That רבי may not hold of מוקצה, which would contradict step 23
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exchange between רבי and his son רבי שמעון about unripe dates, which continues in the next part of the גמרא
